title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section 'Structure à l'infini des M_{g,ν}', a digression on stratified spaces needed to describe the boundary (normal-crossings) structure of compactified moduli spaces.

On the previous page Grothendieck defines, for X a topological space, the presheaf U ↦ Strat_glob(U) of (connected) global stratifications of open subsets. He notes it is not a sheaf: foliations already give an example. Sections of the associated sheaf are called 'structures de stratification locale', by analogy with the local equivalence relations of SGA 4.

On this page he takes such a local stratification structure on X. He supposes, as in the case of foliations (and more generally of all local equivalence relations), that it defines a partition of X into strata (the 'leaves'). Each stratum E carries its own topology, which in general is NOT the induced topology (think of a dense leaf of an irrational linear foliation of the torus). This topology is chosen so that the inclusion E → X (296) is a local immersion, i.e. a local homeomorphism onto a locally closed subspace.

He then defines D*_{Δ0} as the topological sum of all strata ('l'espace somme des feuilles'). The canonical map D*_{Δ0} → X (297) is therefore a continuous bijection and a local immersion; in general it is not a homeomorphism.

On the next page he checks the main example. When the stratification comes from a normal crossings divisor in an analytic space, D*_{Δ0} ≅ ∐_d D*_d, the disjoint union of the loci of points lying on exactly d local branches. This makes the notation compatible with the two preceding sections. The point of the general construction is a canonical 'disjoint union of open strata' object, usable even when strata are only locally defined (non-strict normal crossings, self-intersecting branches, foliation-like behaviour).
errors: The hypothesis that a local stratification defines a global partition into strata, each with a canonical leaf topology, is stated as an assumption ('Supposons…'), not proved. In general, gluing local strata into maximal 'leaves' requires a chain/path-connectedness argument, as for leaves of a foliation; the page leaves this implicit.

Calling (297) 'bijective and a local immersion' is consistent with the leaf topology. It is not a homeomorphism onto X, nor in general an embedding on each stratum. This is correctly flagged by the parenthetical '(qui n'est pas en général la topologie induite)'.

ideas.what: Local stratification = section of the sheafification of the presheaf of global stratifications, by analogy with local equivalence relations
ideas.modern_name: sheaf-theoretic / local stratification structure; cf. singular foliations
ideas.usually_credited_to: no standard credited notion; local equivalence relations in the topos framework go back to Grothendieck (SGA 4)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck refers to SGA 4 (théorie des topos) for local equivalence relations; exact location unsure

ideas.what: Partition into leaves/strata with own (leaf) topology such that inclusion is a local immersion
ideas.modern_name: leaf topology; immersed leaves of a (singular) foliation
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical foliation theory (Ehresmann, Reeb); singular foliations Stefan & Sussmann 1973-74

ideas.what: D*_{Δ0}: topological sum of all strata, with canonical bijective local immersion to X; recovers ∐_d D*_d for normal crossings divisors
ideas.modern_name: disjoint union of open strata ('normalization of the stratification'), cf. boundary strata of Deligne–Mumford compactification
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in the theory of normal crossings / log geometry

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly unifies stratifications and foliations: a 'local stratification' is a sheafified stratification whose strata are immersed leaves with their own topology. This is essentially the framework of Stefan–Sussmann singular foliations, but arrived at from the stratification side and in a topos-theoretic (sheaf of structures) spirit. It was aimed at the boundary of M_{g,ν}.
missed.quote: chaque strate E étant munie d'une topologie (qui n'est pas en général la topologie induite) telle que l'inclusion E → X soit une immersion locale
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Recent work on singular foliations (Androulidakis–Skandalis, Lie algebroids/groupoids) and on stratified spaces/exit paths treats these separately. Grothendieck's sheaf-of-stratifications viewpoint is a modest, apparently unpublished bridge. It is relevant to non-strict normal crossings boundaries of moduli stacks.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful, foundational but fairly routine definitions. The sheafification of stratifications and the analogy with foliations and local equivalence relations is a nice unpublished framing, but the content (leaf topology, sum of strata) is standard.
transcription_corrections: 'plus gén. des tontes les relations' should read 'plus gén. (toutes les relations d'équivalence locale)', i.e. 'toutes'.
'alors que strates E' is most likely 'chaque strate E étant munie d'une topologie'.
'Supposons, au point comme dans le cas' is likely 'Supposons, ce qui est le cas comme dans le cas des feuilletages' (uncertain).
'désigner par D*_{Δ0} l'espace somme des feuilles' — the struck/inserted words are 'l'espace somme'.
Last line: '[…] est bijective, et une imm. locale' — the struck word before 'est' is illegible (possibly 'qui').
